solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No time for prejudice about fringe article that started it all?

indicators.note: the trimmed word for prejudice goes about, i.e. around, the next two pieces
'No' before the word time says that letter is to be dropped from the word for prejudice

parts.note: bigotry is intolerant prejudice
bangs (or a bang) is the American word for a fringe of hair
the definite article

explanation.surface: A grumble that bigotry, with no time spent, has wrapped itself round some trivial fringe item that began everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' drops the time letter from the prejudice word, and 'about' wraps what is left around the fringe and the article. Bangs is the American word for a hair fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmological model says the universe began in one great expansion, so it is the theory of what started everything.

clue.text: 'Live 2001 in Edinburgh' fluttered tiny flyer?

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: fluttered says the letters flap about into a new order

parts.note: 2001 in Roman numerals is MMI

explanation.surface: A concert billed as live from Edinburgh in 2001 apparently set a little bird fluttering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttered' mixes the Roman numerals for 2001 with the city's name; the quotation marks make the start look like a gig title.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban bird is the smallest bird in the world, a tiny flying creature only about five centimetres long.

clue.text: Piggery's good animals from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: deer are animals

explanation.surface: A farmer notes that the pig unit is good for animals brought up from the southern farms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' reverses DEER to REED in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Piggery can mean piggish behaviour, gluttony or avarice, a synonym for grasping excess.

clue.text: Worker getting cold in truck area? He definitely would be here

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

indicators.note: the cold letter goes in the word for truck

parts.note: an artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A labourer complains about the chill in the back of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' refers back to the worker getting cold: the frozen continent is where he would certainly be cold. An ARTIC is a British articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern polar continent is the coldest place on Earth, where any worker would certainly be freezing.

clue.text: Students collectively note piston's fall and rise

parts.note: G is a musical note
a ram is a piston, as in a hydraulic ram

indicators.note: the ram goes down the column and then comes back up, so it appears again written backwards

explanation.surface: Pupils as a body observe how an engine's piston goes down and up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall and rise' writes RAM down the grid then back up as MAR. A grammar is a British selective state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammar school is informally called a grammar, and a school can stand for its students as a body.

clue.text: Some cards put on table, as done by management

parts.note: a hand is the set of cards dealt to a player
in card games to lead is to play the first card on the table

explanation.surface: A card player lays some cards down, in the way bosses operate.
explanation.definitionFit: Management deals with or manages things, so something it did was dealt with or managed.

clue.text: Of late, notice string turning up in spaghetti bolognese

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read upwards, backwards
in says the letters lie within the two words of the dish

explanation.surface: A notice of a string of pasta poking up in a plate of spaghetti bolognese.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters TIBO sit in 'spaghetTI BOlognese'; 'turning up' reverses them. 'string' is a link, pointing to the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a published notice about someone who has died, someone 'late'.

clue.text: One from school's cowardly if climbing on back of dolphin

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the word is reversed
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fish from the shoal is called cowardly for riding on a dolphin's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns IF into FI; 'back of' gives N from dolphin. A 'school' here is a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowfin is a tuna that swims in schools, so it is one member of a school of fish.

clue.text: Foreign corporal pressing for treatment to be relaxed?

parts.note: Swedish is one example of foreign, from abroad
massage is pressing and kneading of the body, corporal meaning bodily

explanation.surface: A foreign army corporal is put under pressure to relax his discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporal' looks like an army rank but here means bodily.
explanation.definitionFit: This style of rubdown with long strokes is a common therapy given to help someone unwind.

clue.text: Outspoken reserve coach is an issue for The Observer

indicators.note: outspoken suggests the word is to be spoken, so we want something that sounds the same

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, reserve
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A newspaper story: an outspoken substitute coach is a problem for The Observer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Observer' looks like the Sunday newspaper but is anyone who observes. ICE, said, sounds like EYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching vision is a problem for someone doing a lot of watching or looking.

clue.text: Not a blood relation, unlike Jesse James?

definitions.meaning: a relative by marriage, not by blood
the American train robber was an outlaw, the opposite of being inside the law

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as 'in law', the reverse of outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative acquired by marriage, such as a mother of a spouse, shares no blood with you.

clue.text: Holding to make most of spin bowler's play in broadcast

indicators.note: holding says the word for the spin bowler contains the next piece

parts.note: Derek Underwood was a famous England spin bowler
to milk a situation is to make the most of it

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: Michael Holding on how a spin bowler exploits his chances in the broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Holding looks like the fast bowler turned commentator Michael Holding; it is the containment signal. Underwood bowled left-arm spin for England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dylan Thomas wrote this drama for radio, first broadcast by the BBC in 1954.

clue.text: See 11
See 11
Still in mess: on top of double one, you need six double sixes!

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits on top of the second
the word for still goes inside the word for mess

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a filthy mess
even can mean still, as in even (still) better
one twice makes two

explanation.surface: A darts or dominoes player still in a mess, needing six double sixes on top of a double one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is an adverb here, as in 'still better'; a sty is a pigsty, hence a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Six double sixes add up to six times twelve, so that number is what you need.

clue.text: Dragon needs start of battle for knight, one in 25

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in for another

parts.note: a dragon is a monster
N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A knight fighting a dragon needs the battle to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The start of battle, B, replaces N (knight) in MONSTER. 25 is GANG (25-down).
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster or criminal thug is one member of a criminal band.

clue.text: Like coal or oil

parts.note: coal is black
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A question of whether a fuel is like coal or oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word but is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude petroleum is nicknamed this because it is dark and immensely valuable.

clue.text: Gallic, this officer's disgracefully mistreated

indicators.note: mistreated says the letters are muddled, the word Gallic also being part of the mixture

parts.note: the letters of this word hold the answer and Gallic together

explanation.surface: A French officer was disgracefully mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: the answer plus GALLIC is an anagram of DISGRACEFULLY. Alfred Dreyfus was the French army officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Dreyfus was the Jewish French army captain falsely convicted in the famous 1890s affair.

clue.text: Snub fancy beds, none being edged with subtle shades

indicators.note: none of the words keeps its edges, so only the middle letters of each remain

explanation.surface: A snub to fancy beds, none of them edged with subtle colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the outer letters of Snub, fancy and beds: NU + ANC + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nuanced has fine distinctions or gradations, small shades of meaning or colour.

clue.text: Proclamation of Law, perhaps, took in D-Day?

indicators.note: a proclamation is said out loud, so we want what the words sound like

parts.note: the actor Jude Law gives Jude, and took in (food) is ate

explanation.surface: A historian asks whether a proclamation of law took in the D-Day landings.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'due' is said 'joo', so 'Jude ate' sounds like the answer. 'D-Day' here is the deadline day, not 1944.
explanation.definitionFit: The day when something is expected or deadline falls can be called its D-Day.

clue.text: Native shot by Frenchman somewhere in Indochina

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A local is gunned down by a Frenchman in colonial Indochina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges NATIVE into VIETNA.
explanation.definitionFit: This country lies on the eastern side of the Southeast Asian peninsula once called French Indochina.

clue.text: More sound volume overlooks a top lady from Windsor

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above, looking down over, the rest

parts.note: a lid is a top
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, who lives at Windsor Castle

explanation.surface: Turning up the volume, a Windsor lady looks down on a top in better voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Windsor Castle is a royal residence, so the lady is the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound means well founded or valid, so more sound is the comparative of valid.

clue.text: Couples in Barbie & Ken's van get hot

indicators.note: couples are pairs, so two letters are taken from each name
the van is the front, so the pairs come from the front of each word

explanation.surface: Barbie and Ken in their camper van get overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: The first pair of letters of each doll's name: BA + KE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bake is to become very hot, as in sitting in the summer sun.

clue.text: Thoroughly shaft

definitions.meaning: a vertical bore sunk into the ground, as for water

explanation.definitionFit: Fully or properly is an adverb sense; the noun sense is a sunk bore for water or oil.

clue.text: Launches lead-free comestibles from 2122?

indicators.note: lead-free says the leading letter is removed

parts.note: to launch is to start, so launches means starts

explanation.surface: A spacecraft launches with lead-free fuel, carrying food from the year 2122.
explanation.walkthrough: 2122 is 21-across + 22-across, BAKE + WELL, the Derbyshire town of Bakewell, famous for its almond pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakewell is famous for its jam and almond pastries, sweet foods from that Derbyshire town.

clue.text: Lively Australian is tense visiting Irishman

indicators.note: the tense letter visits, going inside, the man's name

parts.note: Rory is a typical Irish man's name
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An Australian stays lively though tense while visiting an Irishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rorty is Australian and British slang for boisterous, rowdy and high-spirited fun.

clue.text: Band go to Aberdeen

definitions.meaning: a group of people, a crew
the Scots verb for go, as used in Aberdeen

explanation.definitionFit: A crew of criminals is one sense; the Scots word for walk or travel is the other.

clue.text: Red dictator's concerning Ozzie yob

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating aloud, so we want what the words sound like

parts.note: re means concerning, and an ocker is an uncouth Australian

explanation.surface: A red-blooded dictator is angry about an Australian yob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' looks like a tyrant but is someone speaking for a secretary: RE + OCKER said aloud sounds like the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish wine region is best known for its red wines, so red is an example.

clue.text: Houses vet next to old unfinished Moroccan palace

indicators.note: the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: to vet is to check or audit

indicators.note: unfinished says the last letter is removed

parts.note: a riad is a traditional Moroccan house or palace with a courtyard

explanation.surface: A vet stays next to an old, half-built Moroccan palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' takes D off RIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatres and halls are places that hold audiences, so houses is a theatrical synonym.

clue.text: Chopping head off, dodgy aperture ruined English photo

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked and remade
chopping the head off a word removes its first letter

explanation.surface: A camera with its head chopped off and a dodgy aperture ruined an English photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopping head off' leaves ODGY; 'ruined' shuffles ODGY + APERTURE into DAGUERREOTYP.
explanation.definitionFit: This early photographic process made a picture on a silvered copper plate, so it is a kind of photograph.
